SMTO-EXE-0248 — SMTO can't use the saved Docker login or secret you named

GUID: 050196bf-4078-5281-aefc-a9f0dfa163ba
Slug: docker-secret-reference-invalid
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • The Docker request refers to a saved password, secret or settings file that SMTO couldn't find or that is the wrong kind for this job. Nothing was run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store and find the entry you mentioned. If it is missing, create it with the matching template: Docker registry, Docker secret, or Docker Compose env file. SMTO only accepts the template that fits the job, such as Docker registry for logging in to download or publish images.
  2. In the composer, type @, choose Parameter Store, and pick the exact entry instead of typing its name by hand. Picking it from the list avoids misspellings and names that match more than one entry.
  3. Don't type passwords, tokens or keys as plain settings in your message; save them as a Docker secret and mention that entry. SMTO refuses plain-text settings whose names look like a password, token or key, to keep them private.
  4. For a Docker Compose env file, enter the full path to a file that exists on the Gateway computer, such as /home/alex/app/.env. The file is read on the Gateway computer, so the path must be complete and exist there.

What success looks like

  • SMTO accepts the request and the Docker action runs using your saved login or secret.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, along with the name of the Parameter Store entry, to the person who manages SMTO. Never paste the password or token itself into a message or error report.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A private Docker reference failed: the @reference was missing or matched more than one accepted Parameter, had the wrong profile type (docker_registry, docker_secret, docker_env_file) or an unavailable accepted revision, the env-file path was not an existing absolute Gateway path, or a literal env/build-arg name was classified as secret-bearing.

What this means

  • A private reference was missing/ambiguous, had the wrong typed profile or unavailable accepted revision, an env-file path was invalid, or a public env/build-argument name was classified as secret-bearing. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • A private reference was missing/ambiguous, had the wrong typed profile or unavailable accepted revision, an env-file path was invalid, or a public env/build-argument name was classified as secret-bearing.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect reference type/revision and public field names without revealing values; name-based detection alone does not prove the value is a secret.

How to fix it

  • Create or fix the Parameter Store entry using the matching template (Docker registry for registry_ref, Docker secret for secret_env, Docker Compose env file for env_file_refs, profile_version 1), make sure the key is unique and accepted, use an absolute existing Gateway path for env files, and move secret-looking literal env or build_args values into docker_secret references.
  • Select the exact accepted private profile/reference for the operation and correct invalid private-file paths or public secret-bearing fields.

Retry and execution caution

  • Select an existing accepted private Docker Parameter reference of the required profile type.

How to verify the fix

  • The required accepted typed reference resolves privately and public arguments obey the closed contract.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
